title: Soon by Nick Blaemire at The Loft at St Luke’s #soonthemusical #nickb...
transcript: When the world is literally ending, to what extent is it worth carrying on? That is the central question behind Nick Blaemire's new chamber musical at The Loft at St Luke’s. Charlie is cooped up in her East Village apartment with her fish during the hottest winter on record when Jonah comes along with groceries and a case for living in spite of it all. It sounds grim but it's remarkably cozy and charming once it simmers for a bit. I can't speak to how this was developed, but it seems like something that may have been a concept album first. The plot is a little thin to fill its 90 minutes and it takes a while to get to the heart of things, but the music and the performances shine. Oliver Richman as Jonah is adorably earnest with his affections and his slight overenunciations. He and the rest of the cast make great use of this melodically conversational and pop-infused score. I would have loved more opportunities for them to harmonize with how strong the vocals are. I also couldn't help but yearn for fuller orchestrations, though I enjoyed the intimate and small-scale production. While far from being perfectly constructed, there is a fair amount to enjoy here, from the performances, to the score, to the starring fish. With that, another program for my collection.
classificationReason: First-hand review of Nick Blaemire's chamber musical at The Loft at St Luke's, with specific opinions on the score, performances, plot, and orchestrations.
